panels.title: LIVE (~15s): steps/s, breaks, logs
panels.description: The heartbeat feed — a thin record written every ~15s from the per-step hook, so the run is watchable between segments. Segment records stay the authoritative per-segment observation; this is running totals sampled mid-segment. Separate table, so the two cadences never mix in one series.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, steps_per_s, breaks_total, logs, attack_run FROM heartbeat ORDER BY wall_time
SELECT steps_per_s FROM heartbeat ORDER BY wall_time DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: BREAKS PER LOG  (the scoreboard — history is 399:1)
panels.description: Blocks broken per log obtained. This, not reward, is whether SkyBot is learning the thing it exists to learn. CLAUDE.md §9: 'the reward number has been wrong every single time.' Null means no log has ever dropped.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT breaks_per_log FROM segments WHERE breaks_per_log IS NOT NULL ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Reward concentration (HHI)
panels.description: Herfindahl index over reward sources. 1.0 = one source owns all income, which is what every historical farm looked like: sky 96% of drive, a menu 77% of income. Rising HHI is the early warning.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT reward_hhi FROM segments ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Players online (expect num_envs)
panels.description: Independent server-side truth. On an offline-mode server SkyBot1 is a DIFFERENT player from SkyBot, so a missing whitelist entry shows here as a persistent 1 while the agent's own logs look healthy. -1 means the server was unreachable.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT players_online FROM server ORDER BY wall_time DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Where the reward comes from (top sources, share of gross)
panels.description: The reward ledger's income statement. Shares are over ABSOLUTE amounts, so a source moving a lot of reward in either direction shows up. Source names were READ OFF THE LIVE RUN (symbols/magnet_seek/gaze/novelty/effort), not guessed — the first version named sources that do not exist and every series was empty. If a new source appears, add a json_extract line; the raw map is in reward_shares so nothing is lost meanwhile. First live reading: symbols 62%, magnet_seek 28%, gaze 3%, novelty 3%, effort 1%, hhi 0.46.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, json_extract(reward_shares,'$.symbols') AS symbols, json_extract(reward_shares,'$.magnet_seek') AS magnet_seek, json_extract(reward_shares,'$.gaze') AS gaze, json_extract(reward_shares,'$.novelty') AS novelty, json_extract(reward_shares,'$.effort') AS effort, json_extract(reward_shares,'$.log_break') AS log_break FROM segments ORDER BY wall_time
SELECT wall_time AS time, breaks_total, logs FROM segments ORDER BY wall_time

SELECT je.key AS block, CAST(je.value AS INTEGER) AS broken FROM segments s, json_each(s.breaks_by_type) je WHERE s.seq = (SELECT MAX(seq) FROM segments WHERE breaks_by_type IS NOT NULL AND breaks_by_type != '{}') ORDER BY broken DESC

SELECT je.key AS item, CAST(je.value AS INTEGER) AS crafted FROM segments s, json_each(s.crafts_by_type) je WHERE s.seq = (SELECT MAX(seq) FROM segments WHERE crafts_by_type IS NOT NULL AND crafts_by_type != '{}') ORDER BY crafted DESC

panels.title: Skills: minted vs bound vs refused
panels.description: The competence gate once froze at 16 skills / 0 invocations FOREVER, invisible for days. Minted rising while bound stays flat is that failure returning.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, skills_minted, skills_bound, skills_refused, rssm_no_latent FROM segments ORDER BY wall_time

panels.title: Learning signals (entropy, WM loss, KL, intrinsic)

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, policy_entropy, world_model_loss, kl_divergence, intrinsic_reward, symbolic_decoder_accuracy FROM segments ORDER BY wall_time

panels.description: Read from training_metrics, not from the segment dict. The first version queried policy_entropy/curiosity/world_model_loss out of episode_metrics, where none of them exist, so the panel was empty for a whole run. `curiosity` is not emitted at all — intrinsic_reward is the real signal.

panels.title: Reward + attack behaviour
panels.description: attack_run_max is how long it holds attack without a break. 96% of option activity once went into holding attack on an unreachable trunk, producing 0 logs.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, episode_reward, intrinsic_reward, attack_run_max, attack_run_mean FROM segments ORDER BY wall_time

panels.title: GPU — VRAM by consumer (8 GB card)
panels.description: Device-level, from nvidia-smi on the training host. train_mb is the MineRL/torch process; ollama_mb is the VLM. These two compete for one 8 GB card. Buckets do not sum to mem_used_mb: ~100-200 MB of CUDA context belongs to no process.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, train_mb, ollama_mb, other_mb, vram_used_mb, vram_total_mb FROM host ORDER BY wall_time

panels.title: GPU — utilisation / temp / power
panels.description: util_pct near 100 with a low step rate means the GPU is the bottleneck; util_pct low with a low step rate means it is not.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, util_pct, temp_c, power_w FROM host ORDER BY wall_time

panels.title: THE TRADE: VLM VRAM vs step rate
panels.description: The question this whole feed exists to answer. CLAUDE.md records fovea_interval 12 costing 28% of the step rate; this shows that trade live instead of inferring it. Joined on the nearest 30s bucket because the two feeds have independent cadences (~15s each, unsynchronised).

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT g.t AS time, g.ollama_mb, g.train_mb, h.sps FROM (SELECT CAST(wall_time/30 AS INT)*30 AS t, AVG(ollama_mb) ollama_mb, AVG(train_mb) train_mb  FROM host GROUP BY t) g LEFT JOIN (SELECT CAST(wall_time/30 AS INT)*30 AS t, AVG(steps_per_s) sps  FROM heartbeat GROUP BY t) h ON h.t=g.t ORDER BY g.t

panels.title: HOST — disk % and RAM (the two silent killers)
panels.description: Disk: 256 GB single NVMe, no redundancy, and ALL brain state lives there (world_model.pt, skill bank, break memory) with nothing backed up. RAM: 16 GB, and CLAUDE.md records real RSS exceeding hard_max_gb ALWAYS -- a '2 GB' buffer ceiling measured 3.70 GB. An OOM-kill here is indistinguishable from a crash loop unless you can see this.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT wall_time AS time, disk_pct, mem_used_mb, mem_avail_mb, swap_used_mb FROM host ORDER BY wall_time
